Tiger is the lead of The Last Rebel (TLR), our own original universe. As the hero, he had to carry the whole look of the project: a battle-worn tiger warrior in heavy plate, with glowing runes on the armor, bloodied wraps and a torn red sash.

The sculpt balances animal anatomy with armor that still lets him move, with plates broken up around the shoulders, elbows and knees, and fur, steel, leather and cloth that each read clearly in engine. Like the rest of the TLR cast, he's built for Unreal Engine: channel-packed mask maps drive a master shader, so colors, wear and emissive accents can be changed in engine without re-texturing. The red rune glow is one of those emissive channels.

Need a hero creature that can front a game? This is the level we deliver.

Krishna comes from Man to God (MTG), our own original universe drawn from Indian mythology, alongside Murkaz. We built him as a cinematic digital human: a young Krishna with a calm, confident face, a lean sculpted build, and curly hair grown as real strands.

The jewelry carries a lot of the look: layered gold necklaces, body chains and arm bands set with green stones, all modeled as hard-surface pieces that hold up in close-up. The saffron shawl, sash and dhoti are built in layers for cloth sim, and the hair is an Alembic strand groom, so it moves and catches light naturally in Unreal Engine.

Need a hero or digital human for a story-driven or mythological game? This is the level we deliver.

items.desc:
Murkaz comes from Man to God (MTG), our own original universe drawn from Indian mythology. We built him as a boss-sized brute: heavy frame, braided beard, fur everywhere, and a mace big enough to sell every hit, made to carry a boss fight in gameplay and still hold the camera in a cutscene.

The sculpt does the heavy lifting, with real weight in the belly, shoulders and calves, and leather, cloth and metal that each read differently. Fur trims, beard and hair are alpha cards, so they stay dense and soft without the cost of strand grooms. The lion-head pauldron, carved mace, face paint and embroidered cloth carry most of the surface detail.

Need a mythic boss or a heavy hitter for a dark fantasy game? This is the level we deliver.

items.desc:
We made CHR Skins to show what a cosmetics pipeline looks like when it's built for volume. Every outfit is a set of swappable pieces (top, layer, jeans, shoes) on one shared base body, so new skins come from recombining and retexturing, not rebuilding.

Five base sets (hoodie, shirt, leather jacket, denim jacket and sleeveless denim vest) become 15 distinct looks through color, wash and wear passes. Swap the tops, bottoms and shoes between them and you get hundreds of casual outfits, with fabric that reads as real fleece, cotton and denim at gameplay distance. Topology stays consistent across pieces, so skin weights carry over and everything mixes and matches without clipping.

Need a steady stream of skins for a multiplayer, live-service or streetwear-style game? This is how we'd build it.

items.t: Sir Galahad: The Order 1886 Fan Art
items.desc:
Sir Galahad is our take on the lead knight from The Order: 1886, built from scratch to match a AAA cinematic look. The goal was simple: could our version hold up in the same kind of close-up shots as the original?

The uniform does most of the talking: a wool coat with gold braiding, a leather belt rig with holster and dagger, an embroidered cape emblem, and engraved steel bracers and greaves, each with its own wear and edge breakup. The face and beard are sculpted for close-ups, and the coat and cape are built as clean quad meshes, ready for rigging and cloth sim.

Planning a story-driven action game with period costume? Talk to us about your hero.

Progressive Character Study: "Adam"
Developed internally at Brothers Interactive, "Adam" represents our team's proficiency in creating modular character progression systems, progressive armor tiering, and highly efficient production workflows. This game-ready asset showcases a 5-stage evolutionary pipeline, built from the ground up to demonstrate how a character can seamlessly scale from a base level to an advanced endgame warrior while maintaining strict optimization for low-end performance brackets.

Character Progression Pipeline:
- 1st Level: Base schoolboy archetype.
- 2nd Level: Rebel tier with light guerrilla combat gear additions.
- 3rd Level: Ranged combat specialization featuring specialized bow and arrow equipment.
- 4th Level: Melee combat tier integrating lightweight sword-fighting gear and armor pieces.
- 5th Level: Elite warrior tier fully equipped for one-on-one boss encounters.

Technical Breakdown:
- Budget: Highly optimized low-end triangle budget across all modular tiers
- Texturing: PBR workflow, single 2K base texture map with scalable supporting map slots added per equipment tier requirement
- Target Platforms: Mobile, Nintendo Switch, PC, and Cross-Platform Multiplayer
- Pipeline: Fully optimized with a unified base skeleton and clean deformation topology, engineered for seamless modular attachment swapping, progressive visual upgrades, and fluid integration into real-time gameplay engines.
